title: Forex brokers
author: Far_Boss_4407
selftext:
I’ve been building this bot for the past week off of 2025 data. I’m going to start testing it on 2026 soon and then moving it to actually trading. 

What brokers can I use this bot and what else can I do to let it trade completely for me

comments.author: CrayonsFearMe
comments.body: Alpaca and Tradier are good APIs for trading, Robinhood has an MCP that you can make a py connection for—that’s what I did

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: For forex bots specifically, OANDA and FXCM have decent APIs for automated execution  -  Alpaca is mostly stocks/ETFs, Tradier is US equities and options. The Robinhood MCP approach works but you'll hit rate limits on forex pairs. If you're also looking at stock analysis alongside the forex bot, trademates.co gives structured AI analysis (recommendation, risk class, scenarios) for US equities, not forex or execution. https://trademates.co  -  doesn't touch forex at all, so it's a complement not a replacement. What timeframe is your bot trading?

comments.author: silphotographer
comments.body:
cTrader is pretty nice for your context. I shopped around and it's probably one of the most developer friendly one compared to other typical platforms like MT5. I am running an automated algo via this atm.

1 year isn't the best backtesting approach. If you are extremely confident undergo stress test like Monty Carlos. For example, I went through my algo rigorously to ensure it wasn't overfit or work only favorably in certain trade regime.

If you want some help let me know. Always a sucker to witness trading systems with real edge :)

replies.author: Far_Boss_4407
replies.body: Well I did 2025 because in my head it makes more sense to build it and have it test on the most previous price action. Not something from like 2020. But I tested them on 2025 in a bunch of different ways messing with sessions, stop loss movement and a bunch of other things. My win rate stayed at around 70-74

replies.author: silphotographer
replies.body:
backtesting on one year worth of data screams over fitting to me at worst and regime dependent at best. I have experimented optimization feature for my current working algo that improved my overall return by few percent but the bigger prize was that it reduced the drawdown by half.

  
I thought I was a genius for improving the return without fundamentally altering the spirit of the original algo that proved its worth but alas under 10 year backtesting and additional stress test it overall reduced my sharpie ratio significantly and erodes edge. That one year I tested on happens to work for the new feature but overall it eroded the edge so I had to abandon it. 

I recommend you either look up how to do industry standard of stress testing the algo properly to validate your edge as best as possible or network with someone who can do it for you whom you can trust. In the field where everyone is pumping their chest like that wolf of Wall Street con artist sales broker, it is important to stick to the science and stat that is proven.

  
And even if you do all that you cannot rest easy for your algo may eventually decay and lose the edge over time. Past performance does not necessarily lead to future performance. Even if this becomes crown jewel it will be necessary if you wanna survive and milk this long-term to continue hustling to find non correlated algo with edge so you are more diversified.
